[Rating: 2/10] For a game that's almost entirely random, the rules are pretty complex. Oh well, at least the cards were pretty, even if they were also difficult to hold.

[Rating: 3/10] A little hard to rate, as there are so many variations of rules and scoring systems.  Varying complications of scoring systems exist, but none really matter as the game is completely dominated by luck unless one player is just completely unskilled (or hasn't learned cards or scoring system).  If the cards are stacked favorable to your play, you win.  If not, you lose.  Heck, you can't even actually guarantee a loss no matter how much you try for one.  It's basically War with a thinly veiled disguise to make it look like your play actually matters.

[Rating: 3/10] the polish edition loses a lot of points by saying 2-6 on the box, and then admitting in the rules it's only 2-3. are there any decisions here?

[Rating: 3/10] SOLD IT!  Bought my copy in a Japanese grocery store, I was curious to learn it was Nintendo's first game. Can't say anything about it grabbed me, other than the mystique of being a foreign deck of cards.

[Rating: 3.5/10] [thing=5451][/thing] is card game, of which I played several variations, including a Korean one, that is about set collection and push your luck.  In a lower level, this could easily be called "Top Deck the Game", as the luck in revealing a good card from the top is basically what decides the hands - sure, there are some decisions regarding which Yaku to go after, and, when needed, what to discard, often setting yourself up for the next play. [Rating: 4/10] Let's not kid ourselves, the reason this game has any appeal is 1.) Gambling, and  2.)  Throwing cards at the table as hard as you can.
